body_markdown:
*Anavex now has open INDs in all three core indications: Alzheimer’s disease, Rett syndrome, and Fragile X syndrome*


*Phase 2a study will evaluate the safety, tolerability and pharmacokinetics of blarcamesine oral solution in adult males with Fragile X syndrome*


NEW YORK, NY, October 15, 2026 – Anavex Life Sciences Corp. (“Anavex” or the “Company”), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing innovative treatments for central nervous system diseases with significant unmet medical needs, today announced that it has received notification from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) that the Company may proceed with its planned clinical study under its Investigational New Drug Application (IND) for *ANAVEX®2-73* (blarcamesine) for Fragile X syndrome (FXS), a genetic condition that is the most common inherited cause of intellectual disability and developmental delay and the most commonly known single-gene cause of autism, for which no FDA-approved treatment currently exists. The IND is now open, enabling clinical investigation of blarcamesine in FXS in the United States. Blarcamesine has previously received Orphan Drug Designation from the FDA for the treatment of Fragile X syndrome.


“FDA clearance of the Fragile X IND is an important milestone that gives Anavex open INDs in all three of our core indications: Alzheimer’s Disease, Rett syndrome, and Fragile X syndrome, and supports our continued momentum of working closely with the FDA as we move our programs forward,” stated Terrie Kellmeyer, Ph.D., Interim Chief Executive Officer. “With an open IND, we are positioned to advance ANAVEX2-73-FXS-001, a planned Phase 2a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-ranging study of the safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of blarcamesine oral solution in approximately 60 adult males with FXS, with behavioral (Aberrant Behavior Checklist revised for FXS “ABCFX”) and cognitive (NIH Toolbox) measures included as secondary endpoints. We believe blarcamesine’s differentiated mechanism of action, including its targeting of sigma-1 receptors, uniquely positions Anavex with the potential to pioneer a transformative treatment approach for patients and families affected by Fragile X syndrome. Newly published peer-reviewed data in *Frontiers in Pharmacology* further strengthen the scientific rationale for this program.”


ANAVEX®2-73 (blarcamesine) has been evaluated in the *Fmr1* knockout mouse model of Fragile X syndrome in three peer-reviewed publications, *Scientific Reports* , the *American Journal of Medical Genetics* and most recently *Frontiers in Pharmacology* .


**New Publication in** ***Frontiers in Pharmacology***


The peer-reviewed study, “Blarcamesine improves EEG biomarkers of cortical dysfunction in a mouse model of Fragile X syndrome” published in *Frontiers in Pharmacology* in September 2026, extends the preliminary data Anavex reported in 2024. 14 days of oral blarcamesine produced dose-related improvement in EEG abnormalities, including elevated resting gamma power and impaired synchronization to auditory stimulation, which are shared between the mouse model and individuals with FXS. These EEG biomarker findings support a translational bridge from preclinical research to clinical development in individuals with FXS.


Blarcamesine is an investigational drug that has not been approved by the FDA or any other regulatory authority for any indication, and its safety and efficacy in Fragile X syndrome have not been established.


**About Fragile X Syndrome**


Fragile X syndrome is a genetic disorder caused by a mutation in the *Fmr1* gene located on the X chromosome. This mutation disrupts the production of a protein called FMRP, which is essential for normal brain development and functioning. As a result, individuals with FXS experience a range of cognitive, behavioral, and physical challenges. FXS typically manifests in early childhood, with delayed speech and motor milestones being some of the first noticeable signs. The condition affects both males and females, but males often experience more severe symptoms due to the single X chromosome. While there is no cure for Fragile X syndrome, early intervention and tailored support can help improve outcomes for individuals and their families. An estimated 1 in 7,000 males and 1 in 11,000 females have been diagnosed with FXS. Based on available prevalence estimates, the number of affected individuals could range from approximately 38,000 to 87,000 in the United States and from approximately 777,000 to 1.4 million worldwide (National Fragile X Foundation, 2026).


**About Anavex Life Sciences Corp.**


Anavex Life Sciences Corp. (Nasdaq: AVXL) is a publicly traded clinical stage biopharmaceutical company engaged in the development of novel therapeutics for the treatment of central nervous system diseases with high unmet medical need. Further information is available at www.anavex.com.
